meta.title: Licensed employer, hedged refusal buried mid-posting

payload.requisition_text:
Graduate Software Engineer
Kestrel Dynamics Ltd — Manchester

Kestrel Dynamics develops route-optimisation software for regional bus operators. We are a 40-person company with a 6-person engineering team and a genuinely flat structure.

The programme
Two-year rotation across our scheduling engine (C#/.NET), our driver app (Flutter) and our data team. A dedicated mentor throughout, plus a training budget of £1,500 a year.

Requirements: a numerate degree completed within the last two years, some programming coursework or personal projects, and the ability to explain your thinking clearly. Unfortunately we are not in a position to support visa sponsorship at this time, so please only apply if you already hold the right to work in the UK on a long-term basis. Compensation is £44,500 with annual review each April.

expected.determining_fact: Kestrel Dynamics Ltd holds a Skilled Worker licence, but the posting states it will not support sponsorship for this role.

evidence_anchors.willingness_quote: Unfortunately we are not in a position to support visa sponsorship at this time

design_notes: The refusal is hedged (not in a position to... at this time) and buried inside the requirements paragraph next to right-to-work language. Single-pass readers miss the negation; ground truth is refused, not boilerplate_ambiguous, because the sentence settles the stance.
